name: Law
hook: Assessment that an AI cannot sit for: the student has to speak, be interrupted, and recover.

make.body: Students record oral argument or client counseling in the studio, then annotate their own recording. Production quality matters here: a clean recording makes students confront delivery, pacing and filler in a way a classroom run-through never does.

build.body: An opposing counsel that never gets tired. Students argue a motion against an AI instructed to press the weakest point in their position and to interrupt. The unglamorous benefit is volume: every student gets ten rounds instead of one.

plan.txt: Assign one fact pattern. Students brief it the traditional way. No AI yet.
AI opposing counsel rounds, done as homework, minimum five exchanges. Students submit the transcript with their own margin notes marking where they conceded too fast.
Studio recordings, scheduled in pairs. Ten minutes of argument, five of counseling.
Students watch their own recording against the AI transcript and write a one-page delivery diagnosis. That reflection is the assessment.

prompt: Act as opposing counsel in a moot court exercise for a law student. Here is the fact pattern and my position: [paste]. Your job is to find the weakest link in my argument and attack it repeatedly. Interrupt me when I am being evasive. Do not be collegial, do not concede a point unless I actually earn it, and do not offer to help me improve my argument. Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer.
